source.display_title: 05/18/2026 - Peter Louis x Harry Edmonds — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: London, UK; usually based in Medellin or Tulum

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced anywhere on the call — this rep names Kim explicitly whenever there is one.

prospect.name: Peter Louis
prospect.aka: Josh Thorne — the device label is 'Josh Thorne's iPhone' and the rep addresses him as Josh at 00:23:49. The title name and the in-call name do not match; see the data_integrity flag. Title name retained here as the corpus key.
prospect.location: USA; born in Santa Barbara, California. Current base not stated. Leaving town the following Wednesday.
prospect.occupation: Owner of Quality Billiards and Game Rooms — sales and service of pool tables, shuffleboards, air hockey and game-room equipment. Bought the business roughly seven years ago when it was 48 years old and overhauled it. Previously a professional civilian helicopter pilot for 13 years.
prospect.family_status: Has two children 50% of the time. Implied separated or divorced; not stated.
prospect.training_background: Long history across several modalities — a P90X era, periods of hard gym training, and prior kettlebell work though not to the depth being discussed. Has been at 12-13% body fat once or twice in his life. Currently walks 10,000 steps every morning and attends a CrossFit-hybrid gym he does not enjoy. Has a small home gym with good equipment and prefers to train outside. Had been training about three weeks at the time of the call.
prospect.medical: No conditions disclosed. Reports that heavy axial loading does not suit him — 'the heavy weight compression on my frame is just not really what my body wants' — as a preference rather than a diagnosis. Checks testosterone annually or six-monthly and reports it within range. Takes no supplements; has used creatine in the past.

signals: Successful business owner and former professional pilot; price is explicitly not the barrier — 'I can afford it, but it's not about that'

Self-quantifying and analytical: commissioned a DEXA scan, cross-referenced it against an InBody and a home scale, reasoned about the discrepancy, and set a numeric target of 15% body fat with an option on 12%
Frames the purchase as pushing an already-functioning life further — lean flexibility and vitality into older years, not rescue

Overlay of skeptical_bargain_hunter: he comparison-shopped live against a named competitor and against the company's own $200/month self-guided tier, and asked for testimonials and before-and-afters before committing. He is not price-sensitive but he is evidence-sensitive
He resisted the optimizer label himself — 'I'm probably not good yet' — while describing himself as looking fine with his shirt off and feeling good

goals.text: Get down to 15% body fat from a DEXA-measured 27%, with an option to cut to 12%
Lean flexibility and vitality going into his older years, without becoming a bodybuilder
Rebuild strength, cardio and endurance for life in general
Find and hold a routine he can do at home or outside
Learn proper kettlebell form so he does not injure himself or waste energy
Stop feeling tight, sore and pumped-out from heavy compressive training
Get in and out of the gym and into the office faster
Look good in his birthday suit

pains.text: Unmotivated to go to the gym and dislikes the CrossFit-hybrid style he is currently paying for
Heavy axial loading feels wrong on his frame — 'too much compression'
Business owner with two kids half the time and a social life; time is the binding constraint
Procrastinates and stretches gym time out — 'I kind of putter around and make things take longer than they absolutely need to'
Knows how to cook well but has no time, so struggles to hit protein and buys plastic-packed meal delivery
Cannot get a reliable body-fat reading — 27% on DEXA, 23% on a home scale, 19% on an InBody
Names commitment as his own internal problem — 'it's commitment, right, which is something I got to work on internally'
Concerned about wasting the investment through travel — 'I worry about not just my commitment, but, you know, wasting time via travel'

objections.raw_quote: I mean, there's other programs out there. Like, I found one. You just tell me. You saw that guy out of the UK. You should know him, Shredfast... Well, mean, he has a program, I don't even know what that costs, but I mean, it's the same kind of thing, you're getting kettlebell instruction. It's a similar number. It's less, but you're also not being coached by him.
objections.rep_response: Differentiated on personal delivery — that Shredfast routes buyers to a layer of trained coaches and an app, whereas this is one-to-one with Trevor himself. He supported it with a personal connection ('one of my cousin's friends is Shredfast Coach'). He also affirmed an allegation that the competitor uses steroids. He did not quantify the value of the difference or return to the prospect's own goals.

objections.raw_quote: And what if you don't need all the components like nutrition and all that kind of stuff because you've got it semi-dialed in?
objections.rep_response: Declined to unbundle — 'it's still all included because... we have a system' — and illustrated adaptability with the vegetarian Indian client example. Then immediately offered a one-month trial at $1,200 as the way to resolve the uncertainty.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, a thousand dollars a month is for an elite trainer, right? And I'm not saying Trevor. It's not cheap, obviously, he bills and overhead, and he has to make a living for the hard work he's put in, I worry about not just my commitment, but, you know, wasting time via travel and stuff like that.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed a pause policy exists, then ran the '6,000 reasons to commit' reframe. Did not isolate, did not ask a single financial question, and did not address the travel concern. The prospect then de-isolated it himself: 'I can afford it, but it's not about that.'

objections.raw_quote: All right, well, what are the next steps? You can send me an email with just some of the breakdown or, you know, one month kind of thing, and we can go from there?
objections.rep_response: Agreed without resistance. Described the process as booking the onboarding call once payment is processed, offered to send an overview and testimonials by text, and left it with 'if you've something you want to pursue, hit me up. If not, it's fine.' No objection play was run.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'the guarantee is that by the end of the six months, you will be doing the same movements with the same, uh, intensity, same things with an extra 20 pounds on a kettlebell.' Framed from an example starting weight of 35 pounds. No mention of the work-for-free remediation the rep described on other calls.

prospect_financials.note: Stated plainly that affordability is not the issue — 'I can afford it, but it's not about that.' No financial question was asked and none was needed. The barrier he named was commitment and evidence, not money.

evidence: No commitment of any kind. Closing request was for collateral: 'send me an overview if you can... if you have testimonials or before and afters, I didn't really see any of that on the website. I'd love to check those out.'
No payment taken and no payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply
Timing was pushed out by the prospect: 'I'm leaving town on Wednesday so I won't be starting for another 10 days'

Counter-evidence for a warmer read: he asked detailed buying-stage questions throughout — starting kettlebell weights, hollow versus solid core, whether to use the branded bells, what happens to programming after the term ends — and he was actively weighing the one-month trial
Counter-evidence against: he left holding three cheaper alternatives, two of which the rep supplied — a $1,200 trial, a $200/month self-guided tier, and a named competitor
outcome.next_step: Rep to text or email an overview of the options plus testimonials and before-and-after results. Prospect travelling from Wednesday, would not start for roughly ten days. No follow-up call booked and no date set.

notable.note: The richest pricing and policy call in the batch. Four distinct price points were disclosed — $6,000/6mo and $9,000/12mo as standard, plus a $4,000 three-month tier, a $1,200 one-month trial and a $200/month self-guided product that the rep screen-shared to a prospect he was asking $6,000 from. He also described the trial as routine practice: 'In three months, every person who's done a trial that I've signed up on a trial has continued.' Two ad hoc policies were stated — pauses are permitted, and cancellation 'depends on factors' with a heart attack given as the illustrative case. He additionally disclosed internal company metrics to a prospect who is himself a business owner: roughly 120 active one-to-one clients, a cap around 150, and a team of about twelve including four salespeople. Separately, the mention of 'a weekly workout, which is more group, which is a live session with other clients' contradicts what the same rep told Luis Ortiz two days earlier, that the programme includes no calls at all. Process-wise this was the thinnest call in the batch: price landed at eight minutes with no commitment check, no consequence frame, no past-attempts work and one of nine baseline checks completed. This is also the only prospect in the batch who sits squarely inside the stated ICP, and he is the one who did not buy.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained, worse than average because the prospect's label is a device name. The opening is inverted — 'I'm from London... I'm in London right now, but I usually am in either Medellin or Tulum' is attributed to the prospect but is unmistakably the rep, who is elsewhere confirmed as London-based and Tulum-bound. The entire offer walkthrough from 00:11:11 to 00:14:15 alternates wrongly, with the rep's pillar descriptions landing under the prospect label. The price quotes at 00:11:11, 00:14:48 and 00:23:32 all sit under the wrong speaker. The scoliosis disclosure at 00:25:37 is the rep's own, answering the prospect's question about what he has gained from kettlebells, not a prospect medical disclosure. Roles read from content throughout.
